label: TMUA 2023 · Paper 1 · Question 15

hints.title: Find the input range of the exponential
hints.body: Start from the attainable cosine interval. For a positive base, determine which input gives each extreme output, considering both sides of base one.
hints.recap: An exponential increases for a base above one and decreases for a base between zero and one.
hints.pitfall: Do not assume the named base exceeds one merely because it is positive.
hints.pause: Express the two extreme outputs in terms of a.

recall.reminder: An exponential increases for a base above one and decreases for a base between zero and one.

hints.title: Express an unsigned separation
hints.body: Set the absolute difference of your extreme outputs equal to the required separation. Split the absolute-value equation into its possible signs.
hints.recap: Range separation is maximum minus minimum and is nonnegative.
hints.pitfall: Multiplying by a is safe because a is positive, but negative roots still fail the domain.
hints.pause: Solve each case, check the original positive-base restrictions and add the distinct permitted values.

recall.reminder: Range separation is maximum minus minimum and is nonnegative.

solution:
1. Find the extreme outputs. Cosine attains every value between −1 and 1. The endpoint outputs are a and 1/a; their order depends on whether a is above or below 1. For a=1 the difference is zero, so it cannot work.

2. Use the required separation. |a−1/a|=3. If a>1, then a2−3a−1=0, whose positive root is (3+13)/2. If 0<a<1, then a2+3a−1=0, whose positive root is (−3+13)/2. Each root satisfies its stated case.

3. Add the possible bases. The sum is 13. Answer F.
knowledgePattern: Split the exponential range separation into reciprocal-base cases
